title: Thor and Loki (Norse mythology)
subtitle: Norse mythology
subject: mythologie
description: The god of thunder and the god of trickery: partners in adventure, then enemies at Ragnarok. Two faces of the Norse pantheon.

hero.hook: One strikes with a hammer. The other lies to win. Together they save Asgard, until the day Loki turns on it.

blocks.text: **Thor** and **Loki** are the two most popular figures in Norse mythology. Thor protects people with lightning. Loki spreads disorder with cunning. The travel stories often show them side by side.

Their bond is more than a comic friendship. It holds the tension between the order of the gods and chaos. From prankish partnership to the final war, here is how the alliance is built and then broken.

These myths come from the Scandinavian peoples of the 5th to the 12th century. We know them mostly through late Icelandic texts, written when the region was already Christian. The main source is the [[Prose Edda]], written around **1220** by **Snorri Sturluson**, alongside the [[Poetic Edda]].

blocks.caption: Asgard and Midgard joined by Bifrost, the rainbow bridge

blocks.text: The world is arranged around [[Yggdrasil]], the cosmic tree. At the top sits **Asgard**, home of the gods. Lower down lies **Midgard**, the world of humans, linked by the **Bifrost**. The gods split into two clans: the **Aesir**, led by **Odin** (war and rule), and the **Vanir**, such as Freyr and Freyja (fertility).
In the old texts, Bifrost is a fragile bridge: at Ragnarok it will shake and break under the weight of the giants.

sections.title: Thor, the protector with the hammer

blocks.text: **Thor** is the son of Odin and the Earth. He is the god ordinary people worshipped most: he defends humanity against the **giants**, the wild forces of nature. Bearded and red-haired, he stands for plain, straightforward strength.

blocks.caption: Mjolnir, the hammer of Thor: it strikes and comes back to his hand

blocks.text: His weapon, **Mjolnir**, forged by dwarves, splits mountains and always flies back to his hand. A belt of strength and iron gloves help him handle it. His name gave the Germanic languages **Thursday**, Thor's day. Odin is the more aristocratic god; Thor belongs to the free farmers: rain, harvest, a safe home.
Thor's chariot is pulled by two goats. If he is hungry he can eat them at night and bring them back to life the next morning with his hammer, as long as nobody breaks a bone.

sections.title: Loki, the cunning that ends badly

blocks.text: **Loki** lives among the Aesir, but his blood is giant blood. He joined the pantheon through a blood pact with Odin. He is the **trickster**: his pranks and lies cause trouble, yet they also push the story forward and sometimes hand the gods their greatest treasures.

blocks.caption: Loki, god of cunning: a useful ally and a promised traitor

blocks.text: He changes shape and even sex. As a mare he becomes the mother of [[Sleipnir]], Odin's eight-legged horse. With the giantess Angrboda he fathers three monsters: the wolf **Fenrir**, the serpent **Jormungandr**, and **Hel**, keeper of the dead. Step by step the prank turns into betrayal: he arranges the death of the shining god **Baldr**. From then on his fate is sealed.

For a long time Thor and Loki complete each other. When the giant Thrym steals Mjolnir, Thor dresses up as a bride and Loki as her maid to get it back. Where the hammer fails, the lie works, and the other way around.

Then the alliance breaks. At **Ragnarok**, the twilight of the gods, Loki leads the enemies of Asgard. Thor faces Jormungandr, Loki's son: he kills the serpent, then dies of its venom nine steps later. Strength and cunning destroy each other.

**Thor** and **Loki** embody the tension between protective strength and disruptive cunning. Their bond, from comic friendship to the hatred of Ragnarok, shows how fragile the order of the gods is against chaos.
